05-01.title: Duke of Wellington
05-01.description: British military commander and statesman who defeated Napoleon at Waterloo and served twice as Prime Minister, reshaping European history.

05-01.title: Wes Anderson
05-01.description: American filmmaker whose precisely symmetrical, pastel-hued worlds in films like The Grand Budapest Hotel created an instantly recognizable cinematic language.

05-01.title: Calamity Jane
05-01.description: Frontier scout and sharpshooter of the American West whose wild exploits and friendship with Wild Bill Hickok made her a legend of the frontier era.

05-01.title: Acts of Union — Great Britain Formed
05-01.description: England and Scotland were officially united into a single sovereign state, the Kingdom of Great Britain, with one Parliament at Westminster.

05-01.title: Great Exhibition Opens
05-01.description: Queen Victoria opened the world's first international trade fair inside the iconic Crystal Palace in Hyde Park, London, showcasing industrial wonders.

05-01.title: Pluto Named
05-01.description: The newly discovered ninth planet was officially christened Pluto, following a suggestion from Venetia Burney, an eleven-year-old schoolgirl from Oxford.

05-01.title: "I Walk the Line" — Johnny Cash
05-01.description: Cash's vow of fidelity driven by a hypnotic, guitar-string-retuned drone became his first Billboard country number one and a bedrock of American roots music.

05-01.title: Legally Blonde
05-01.description: Reese Witherspoon's Elle Woods proved that a Harvard Law degree and a pink wardrobe are not mutually exclusive in this sharp comedy about underestimation.

05-02.title: Catherine the Great
05-02.description: Russia's longest-ruling female monarch who led the empire to new heights of power and culture, championing Enlightenment reforms and expanding Russian territory.

05-02.title: Dwayne Johnson
05-02.description: Professional wrestler turned global Hollywood star whose charisma and work ethic turned him into one of the highest-paid actors in cinema history.

05-02.title: Satyajit Ray
05-02.description: Indian filmmaker whose Apu Trilogy brought the beauty and sorrow of rural Bengal to the world, earning him an Honorary Academy Award for lifetime achievement.

05-02.title: King James Bible First Published
05-02.description: The landmark English translation of the Bible commissioned by King James I was first published in London, shaping the English language for centuries.

05-02.title: Lou Gehrig Ends Consecutive Games Streak
05-02.description: The Iron Horse removed himself from the lineup after 2,130 consecutive games, ending a record that stood until Cal Ripken Jr. broke it in 1995.

05-02.title: General Motors Acquires Chevrolet
05-02.description: Industrialist Billy Durant orchestrated the deal that brought Chevrolet under the General Motors umbrella, consolidating his automotive empire.

05-02.title: "ABC" — The Jackson 5
05-02.description: Young Michael Jackson led his brothers through this irresistibly bouncy Motown anthem about the simplicity of love, knocking the Beatles off the number one spot.

05-02.title: Selma
05-02.description: Ava DuVernay's stirring drama chronicles Martin Luther King Jr.'s 1965 Selma-to-Montgomery voting rights marches and the fierce struggle behind them.

05-03.title: James Brown
05-03.description: The Godfather of Soul whose explosive live performances and rhythmic innovations in funk became the foundation for hip-hop, R&B, and modern popular music.

05-03.title: Niccolò Machiavelli
05-03.description: Florentine diplomat and political philosopher whose bluntly pragmatic treatise The Prince forever changed how the world thinks about power and statecraft.

05-03.title: Golda Meir
05-03.description: Iron-willed Israeli stateswoman who rose from a Milwaukee school teacher to become the fourth Prime Minister of Israel, leading her nation through the Yom Kippur War.

05-03.title: Margaret Thatcher Elected Prime Minister
05-03.description: The Conservative leader became the first woman to serve as British Prime Minister, ushering in a decade of transformative and controversial economic reform.

05-03.title: Sears Tower Completed
05-03.description: The 108-floor Chicago skyscraper was topped out as the tallest building in the world, a title it held for nearly 25 years before being renamed the Willis Tower.

05-03.title: Adolphe Sax Patents the Saxophone
05-03.description: Belgian inventor Adolphe Sax received a patent for his newly designed woodwind instrument, which would go on to define the sound of jazz and popular music.

05-03.title: "Ticket to Ride" — The Beatles
05-03.description: John Lennon's dense, heavy guitar sound and the song's ambiguous melancholy marked a decisive shift toward the more complex Beatles records to come.

05-03.title: Iron Man 3
05-03.description: Shane Black's witty and action-packed Marvel blockbuster stripped Tony Stark of his armor and forced him to rely on his ingenuity alone.

05-04.title: Audrey Hepburn
05-04.description: Belgian-born actress and humanitarian whose luminous elegance in Breakfast at Tiffany's and Roman Holiday made her one of cinema's most enduring icons.

05-04.title: Randy Travis
05-04.description: Country singer whose velvet baritone and traditional honky-tonk style almost single-handedly revived classic country music in the mid-1980s.

05-04.title: Thomas Huxley
05-04.description: English biologist and fierce champion of Charles Darwin's theory of evolution, so dogged in defending it that he earned the nickname Darwin's Bulldog.

05-04.title: Kent State Shootings
05-04.description: Ohio National Guardsmen opened fire on unarmed student protesters at Kent State University, killing four and wounding nine in a moment that galvanized antiwar sentiment.

05-04.title: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences Founded
05-04.description: Thirty-six of Hollywood's most prominent figures gathered in Los Angeles to establish the institution that would present the Academy Awards.

05-04.title: Rhode Island Renounces King George III
05-04.description: Rhode Island became the first American colony to formally renounce allegiance to the British Crown, two months before the Declaration of Independence.

05-04.title: "Superstition" — Stevie Wonder
05-04.description: Stevie Wonder's thumping, clavinet-driven funk masterpiece was originally written for Jeff Beck and became one of the definitive recordings of the decade.

05-04.title: Star Wars: The Phantom Menace
05-04.description: George Lucas returned to a galaxy far, far away after sixteen years, and the most anticipated sequel in Hollywood history shattered opening-weekend box office records.

05-05.title: Karl Marx
05-05.description: German philosopher and economist whose Communist Manifesto and Das Kapital fundamentally shaped the political landscape of the twentieth century.

05-05.title: Adele
05-05.description: British singer-songwriter whose powerfully emotive voice and candid songwriting on albums like 21 and 25 made her one of the best-selling artists of all time.

05-05.title: Nellie Bly
05-05.description: Pioneering investigative journalist who feigned insanity to expose the brutal conditions inside New York's Blackwell Island asylum and then raced around the world in 72 days.

05-05.title: Battle of Puebla — Cinco de Mayo
05-05.description: A outnumbered Mexican army stunned Napoleon III's elite French forces at Puebla, a victory that became a symbol of Mexican national pride celebrated as Cinco de Mayo.

05-05.title: Chanel No. 5 Released
05-05.description: Coco Chanel released her groundbreaking perfume, the first to bear a designer's name and destined to become the most iconic fragrance in history.

05-05.title: Alan Shepard Becomes First American in Space
05-05.description: Astronaut Alan Shepard made a 15-minute suborbital flight aboard Freedom 7, becoming the first American to travel into space.

05-05.title: Stranger in Town — Bob Seger
05-05.description: Bob Seger's heartland rock triumph produced Old Time Rock and Roll and Still the Same, cementing his status as a voice for working-class America.

05-05.title: The Avengers
05-05.description: Joss Whedon united Iron Man, Thor, Captain America, and the Hulk in a wildly entertaining superhero ensemble that became the third highest-grossing film of all time.

05-06.title: Sigmund Freud
05-06.description: Austrian neurologist who founded psychoanalysis, forever changing how humanity understands the unconscious mind, dreams, and human motivation.

05-06.title: Willie Mays
05-06.description: Electrifying center fielder of the New York and San Francisco Giants whose breathtaking over-the-shoulder catch in the 1954 World Series remains baseball's greatest defensive play.

05-06.title: George Clooney
05-06.description: Charming Hollywood actor and filmmaker who parlayed ER stardom into an Oscar-winning career spanning Ocean's Eleven, Michael Clayton, and Gravity.

05-06.title: Hindenburg Disaster
05-06.description: The German passenger airship LZ 129 Hindenburg burst into flames while landing in New Jersey, killing 36 people and ending the era of hydrogen-filled rigid airships.

05-06.title: Roger Bannister Breaks Four-Minute Mile
05-06.description: British medical student Roger Bannister ran a mile in 3:59.4 at Oxford, shattering a barrier that many had considered physiologically impossible.

05-06.title: Channel Tunnel Opens
05-06.description: Queen Elizabeth II and French President François Mitterrand officially inaugurated the undersea rail tunnel linking Britain to continental Europe beneath the English Channel.

05-06.title: Damn. — Kendrick Lamar
05-06.description: Kendrick Lamar's Pulitzer Prize-winning rap opus debuted at number one and went on to become the first non-classical, non-jazz record to receive the prize.

05-06.title: The Dark Knight
05-06.description: Christopher Nolan's operatic crime thriller gave Heath Ledger's Joker a posthumous Oscar and redefined what a superhero film could achieve artistically.

05-07.title: Johannes Brahms
05-07.description: German Romantic composer whose four symphonies, piano concertos, and German Requiem represent the summit of nineteenth-century absolute music.

05-07.title: Rabindranath Tagore
05-07.description: Bengali polymath poet, playwright, and painter who became the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his spiritual verse collection Gitanjali.

05-07.title: Eva Perón
05-07.description: Argentina's beloved First Lady who championed women's suffrage, labor rights, and social welfare with a passion that made her an enduring icon of populism.

05-07.title: Beethoven's 9th Symphony Premieres
05-07.description: The profoundly deaf composer's final symphony premiered in Vienna to thunderous applause, its choral finale Ode to Joy later becoming the anthem of the European Union.

05-07.title: RMS Lusitania Sunk
05-07.description: A German U-boat torpedoed the British ocean liner off the coast of Ireland, killing 1,198 people including 128 Americans and hardening U.S. public opinion against Germany.

05-07.title: Germany Signs World War II Surrender
05-07.description: German military commanders signed an unconditional surrender at Reims, France, ending nearly six years of devastating war in Europe.

05-07.title: "Hotel California" — Eagles
05-07.description: The Eagles' haunting meditation on excess and the dark side of the American dream peaked at number one and became one of the greatest rock songs ever recorded.

05-07.title: Notorious
05-07.description: Alfred Hitchcock directed Cary Grant and Ingrid Bergman in this espionage thriller set in postwar Rio, featuring one of cinema's most celebrated kisses.

05-08.title: Harry S. Truman
05-08.description: The 33rd U.S. President who made the momentous decision to drop atomic bombs on Japan, issued the Marshall Plan, and desegregated the American armed forces.

05-08.title: David Attenborough
05-08.description: British naturalist and broadcaster whose Planet Earth documentaries brought the majesty and fragility of the natural world to billions of television viewers.

05-08.title: Enrique Iglesias
05-08.description: Spanish singer who followed in his father's footsteps to become the undisputed King of Latin Pop, with record-breaking runs on the Billboard Latin chart.

05-08.title: VE Day — World War II Ends in Europe
05-08.description: Victory in Europe Day marked the formal acceptance of Nazi Germany's unconditional surrender, sending millions of jubilant crowds into the streets across Allied nations.

05-08.title: Smallpox Declared Eradicated
05-08.description: The World Health Organization officially declared smallpox eradicated, marking humanity's first and to date only complete elimination of a human infectious disease.

05-08.title: Paramount Pictures Founded
05-08.description: Adolph Zukor and Jesse Lasky founded what would become one of Hollywood's most storied studios, responsible for Godfather, Chinatown, and countless classics.

05-08.title: Let It Be — The Beatles
05-08.description: The Beatles' final studio album, a raw document of their disintegration, was released just weeks after Paul McCartney announced he was leaving the band.

05-08.title: Speed Racer
05-08.description: The Wachowskis crafted a deliriously colorful live-action adaptation of the classic anime series that was panned on release but became a cult favorite.

05-09.title: Billy Joel
05-09.description: The Piano Man himself, a Long Island-born singer-songwriter whose confessional pop anthems and barnstorming live shows made him one of the best-selling artists ever.

05-09.title: Mike Wallace
05-09.description: Ferocious 60 Minutes journalist whose confrontational interview style held presidents, dictators, and corporate leaders to a standard of unflinching accountability.

05-09.title: Glenda Jackson
05-09.description: British actress who won two Academy Awards for Best Actress before abandoning Hollywood for a distinguished career as a Labour Member of Parliament.

05-09.title: First Mother's Day Proclaimed
05-09.description: President Woodrow Wilson issued a proclamation designating the second Sunday of May as Mother's Day, a national day of honor that spread worldwide.

05-09.title: First Aircraft Over the North Pole
05-09.description: Explorer Richard Byrd and pilot Floyd Bennett completed a daring flight over the geographic North Pole in a Fokker trimotor, the first such aerial crossing.

05-09.title: John Brown's Raid on Pottawatomie
05-09.description: Abolitionist John Brown led a midnight raid killing five pro-slavery settlers in Kansas, escalating the Bleeding Kansas conflict that foreshadowed the Civil War.

05-09.title: Electronic Sound — George Harrison
05-09.description: The first Beatle to release a solo album, Harrison's experimental Moog synthesizer record on the Zapple label was a radical departure from the Fab Four sound.

05-09.title: Star Trek
05-09.description: J.J. Abrams rebooted the beloved franchise with a time-travel origin story that introduced a new generation to Kirk and Spock while thrilling longtime fans.

05-10.title: Fred Astaire
05-10.description: American dancer and actor whose gravity-defying Fred and Ginger films set the standard for elegance, and whose innovative choreography changed the art form forever.

05-10.title: Bono
05-10.description: Lead singer of U2 whose soaring tenor voice, arena-filling ambition, and tireless humanitarian campaigns have made him one of the most influential figures in rock history.

05-10.title: Maurice Sendak
05-10.description: American author and illustrator whose Where the Wild Things Are opened the door to darker, more emotionally honest storytelling in children's literature.

05-10.title: First Transcontinental Railroad Completed
05-10.description: The Central Pacific and Union Pacific tracks were joined at Promontory Summit, Utah, with a golden spike uniting the continent by rail for the first time.

05-10.title: Nelson Mandela Inaugurated as President
05-10.description: After 27 years in prison, Nelson Mandela was inaugurated as South Africa's first democratically elected president, marking the end of apartheid.

05-10.title: Winston Churchill Becomes Prime Minister
05-10.description: On the same day Germany launched its assault on Western Europe, King George VI asked Winston Churchill to form a government and lead Britain through the war.

05-10.title: Are You Experienced — Jimi Hendrix Experience
05-10.description: Jimi Hendrix's electrifying debut album rewired rock guitar forever, featuring Purple Haze, Hey Joe, and a studio experimentation that still sounds futuristic.

05-10.title: Gladiator
05-10.description: Ridley Scott's sword-and-sandal epic restored the Roman epic to the mainstream and won Russell Crowe the Academy Award for Best Actor.

05-11.title: Salvador Dalí
05-11.description: Flamboyant Spanish surrealist painter whose melting clocks and dreamlike landscapes in The Persistence of Memory made him the most recognizable artist of the 20th century.

05-11.title: Andrés Iniesta
05-11.description: Spanish midfield maestro whose precise passing and intelligent movement drove Barcelona's tiki-taka dominance and delivered Spain its first World Cup title in 2010.

05-11.title: Harriet Quimby
05-11.description: American journalist and aviator who became the first woman to earn a U.S. pilot's licence and the first woman to fly solo across the English Channel in 1912.

05-11.title: Constantine Dedicates Constantinople
05-11.description: Emperor Constantine the Great renamed the rebuilt city of Byzantium as Nova Roma, establishing it as the new imperial capital of the Roman Empire.

05-11.title: Dust Bowl Begins
05-11.description: A massive dust storm darkened the skies over the Great Plains, heralding the Dust Bowl ecological disaster that drove hundreds of thousands of farming families from their homes.

05-11.title: Israel Admitted to the United Nations
05-11.description: Just over a year after declaring independence, the State of Israel was accepted as the 59th member of the United Nations.

05-11.title: "What's Going On" — Marvin Gaye
05-11.description: Marvin Gaye's landmark soul protest album, released against Motown's wishes, addressed Vietnam and racial injustice and is widely regarded as the greatest album of all time.

05-11.title: Black Hawk Down
05-11.description: Ridley Scott's visceral recreation of the 1993 Battle of Mogadishu immerses viewers in the chaos of urban combat with relentless, unflinching intensity.

05-12.title: Florence Nightingale
05-12.description: English social reformer who revolutionized nursing during the Crimean War, her lamp-lit nighttime ward rounds earning her the enduring title Lady with the Lamp.

05-12.title: Yogi Berra
05-12.description: Beloved New York Yankees catcher and ten-time World Series champion whose malapropistic Yogi-isms became as legendary as his Hall of Fame career.

05-12.title: George Carlin
05-12.description: Counterculture stand-up comedian whose Seven Words You Can't Say on Television routine went to the U.S. Supreme Court and made him a champion of free speech.

05-12.title: Soviet Blockade of West Berlin Lifted
05-12.description: After 11 months of the Berlin Airlift delivering over 2.3 million tons of supplies by air, the Soviet Union lifted its blockade of the divided city.

05-12.title: First Undisputed Flight Over the North Pole
05-12.description: Roald Amundsen, Lincoln Ellsworth, and Umberto Nobile completed the first verified transpolar flight in the airship Norge, crossing from Svalbard to Alaska.

05-12.title: First Ice Cream Advertisement
05-12.description: Philip Lenzi placed an advertisement in the New York Gazette offering ice cream for sale, making it the first documented ice cream advertisement in America.

05-12.title: Exile on Main St. — The Rolling Stones
05-12.description: Recorded in a sweltering basement in the south of France, the Stones' sprawling double album is considered one of the greatest rock records ever made.

05-12.title: The Great Gatsby
05-12.description: Baz Luhrmann's glittering, anachronistic adaptation of Fitzgerald's novel turned the Jazz Age into a hypnotic spectacle of excess and longing.

05-13.title: Stevie Wonder
05-13.description: Blind from birth, Stevie Wonder became a Motown prodigy at 11 and one of the most gifted musicians of any era, a master of piano, harmonica, and studio craft.

05-13.title: Stephen Colbert
05-13.description: Satirist and late-night host whose Comedy Central character and Late Show tenure turned political satire into a nightly art form watched by millions.

05-13.title: Maria Theresa
05-13.description: Habsburg Empress and Queen of Hungary and Bohemia who ruled for forty years, instituting sweeping reforms and becoming one of history's most capable monarchs.

05-13.title: Brazil Abolishes Slavery
05-13.description: Princess Isabel signed the Lei Áurea, the Golden Law, freeing approximately 700,000 enslaved people and making Brazil the last country in the Americas to abolish slavery.

05-13.title: Pope John Paul II Survives Assassination Attempt
05-13.description: Turkish gunman Mehmet Ali Ağca shot Pope John Paul II twice in St. Peter's Square; the Pope survived and later personally forgave his attacker in prison.

05-13.title: First Formula One World Championship Race
05-13.description: The inaugural Formula One World Championship race was held at Silverstone, won by Italian driver Giuseppe Farina in an Alfa Romeo.

05-13.title: Brothers in Arms — Dire Straits
05-13.description: Dire Straits' fifth album became one of the first CDs to sell a million copies and introduced the guitar epic Money for Nothing to a global audience.

05-13.title: Star Trek: Into Darkness
05-13.description: J.J. Abrams' adrenaline-soaked sequel pitted the crew of the Enterprise against Benedict Cumberbatch's menacing villain in a breathless blockbuster.

05-14.title: George Lucas
05-14.description: American filmmaker who created Star Wars and Indiana Jones, transforming Hollywood's relationship with blockbusters, special effects, and merchandise forever.

05-14.title: Mark Zuckerberg
05-14.description: Harvard dropout who co-founded Facebook in his dormitory room and built it into a social media empire connecting more than three billion people worldwide.

05-14.title: Cate Blanchett
05-14.description: Australian actress regarded as one of the finest performers of her generation, a two-time Academy Award winner known for her transformative range and screen presence.

05-14.title: State of Israel Declared
05-14.description: David Ben-Gurion proclaimed the establishment of the State of Israel just hours before the British Mandate expired, triggering the first Arab-Israeli War.

05-14.title: First Smallpox Vaccination
05-14.description: British physician Edward Jenner inoculated 8-year-old James Phipps with cowpox material, establishing the principle of vaccination and saving hundreds of millions of lives.

05-14.title: Skylab Launched
05-14.description: NASA launched its first space station, Skylab, into orbit aboard a Saturn V rocket, where it hosted three crews of astronauts over the following nine months.

05-14.title: Lemonade — Beyoncé
05-14.description: Beyoncé's visual album dropped without warning and sent all twelve tracks simultaneously onto the Billboard Hot 100, a feat unprecedented for a female artist.

05-14.title: Alien
05-14.description: Ridley Scott's terrifying space-set horror film introduced the world to Sigourney Weaver's Ripley and a creature design by H.R. Giger that haunts dreams to this day.

05-15.title: L. Frank Baum
05-15.description: American author who conjured the land of Oz in The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, creating an enduring fantasy universe that has never left the popular imagination.

05-15.title: Brian Eno
05-15.description: British musician and producer who pioneered ambient music and shaped the sound of David Bowie, U2, and Talking Heads through his revolutionary studio work.

05-15.title: Eddy Merckx
05-15.description: Belgian cycling legend nicknamed The Cannibal who won the Tour de France five times, the Giro d'Italia five times, and is considered the greatest cyclist of all time.

05-15.title: National Woman Suffrage Association Founded
05-15.description: Susan B. Anthony and Elizabeth Cady Stanton founded the NWSA in New York, launching a dedicated campaign for women's right to vote that culminated in the 19th Amendment.

05-15.title: Las Vegas Founded
05-15.description: The town of Las Vegas, Nevada was officially established when 110 acres of land were auctioned off, planting the seed for what would become the world's entertainment capital.

05-15.title: First Airline Stewardess on Duty
05-15.description: Ellen Church became the world's first flight attendant when she and seven nurses began serving passengers on United Airlines routes between Oakland and Chicago.

05-15.title: Play — Moby
05-15.description: Moby's fifth album, built on haunting samples of old gospel and blues field recordings, became the best-selling electronic album of all time with 12 million copies sold.

05-15.title: Mad Max: Fury Road
05-15.description: George Miller's kinetic, feminist-charged post-apocalyptic chase film swept six Academy Awards and is considered one of the greatest action films ever made.

05-16.title: Janet Jackson
05-16.description: Pop and R&B superstar who stepped out of her famous family's shadow with Control and Rhythm Nation 1814, albums that made her a defining voice of her generation.

05-16.title: Pierce Brosnan
05-16.description: Irish actor who brought suave charisma to James Bond across four films and proved his dramatic depth in films like The Thomas Crown Affair.

05-16.title: Liberace
05-16.description: Flamboyant American pianist and entertainer whose rhinestone suits and candelabra-topped piano became the ultimate symbols of theatrical showmanship.

05-16.title: First Academy Awards Ceremony
05-16.description: The very first Oscars ceremony was held at the Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel in Los Angeles, with 270 guests and a ceremony that lasted just fifteen minutes.

05-16.title: First Laser Fired
05-16.description: American physicist Theodore Maiman successfully operated the world's first laser at the Hughes Research Laboratories, firing a pulse of ruby-red light that changed science.

05-16.title: Andrew Johnson Acquitted at Impeachment Trial
05-16.description: The U.S. Senate voted 35-19 to convict President Johnson, one vote short of the required two-thirds majority, allowing him to remain in office.

05-16.title: Pet Sounds — The Beach Boys
05-16.description: Brian Wilson's orchestral pop masterpiece, a teenage symphony to God, inspired the Beatles to make Sgt. Pepper and is still ranked among the greatest albums ever recorded.

05-16.title: The Big Lebowski
05-16.description: The Coen Brothers' shaggy stoner noir, dismissed on release, became one of cinema's greatest cult films and launched an annual festival known as Lebowski Fest.

05-17.title: Erik Satie
05-17.description: Eccentric French composer whose Gymnopédies and Gnossiennes pioneered minimalism and ambient music, influencing generations of composers and filmmakers.

05-17.title: Dennis Hopper
05-17.description: Rebel American actor and director whose road-trip counterculture film Easy Rider defined a generation and whose unpredictable intensity electrified every role he played.

05-17.title: Sugar Ray Leonard
05-17.description: One of the greatest boxers of the twentieth century, the Olympic gold medalist won world titles in five weight classes with a combination of speed, skill, and showmanship.

05-17.title: Brown v. Board of Education Decided
05-17.description: The U.S. Supreme Court issued a unanimous ruling declaring racial segregation in public schools unconstitutional, a seismic moment in the civil rights movement.

05-17.title: Watergate Senate Hearings Begin
05-17.description: Televised Senate hearings into the Watergate break-in began, transfixing the nation over the summer and leading to President Nixon's resignation fourteen months later.

05-17.title: Massachusetts Legalizes Same-Sex Marriage
05-17.description: Massachusetts became the first U.S. state to legally recognize same-sex marriages, issuing licences to thousands of couples in a landmark moment for civil rights.

05-17.title: Brothers in Arms — Dire Straits
05-17.description: Dire Straits' platinum juggernaut became one of the first albums to sell one million copies on CD, its sweeping guitar sound filling arenas worldwide.

05-17.title: Shrek
05-17.description: DreamWorks' irreverent animated fairy tale subverted every Disney convention with earthy humor, a lovable ogre, and a talking donkey voiced by Eddie Murphy.

05-18.title: Pope John Paul II
05-18.description: The Polish pope who served 26 years and became a powerful moral force against communism, his visit to his homeland helping spark the Solidarity movement that brought down Soviet rule.

05-18.title: Bertrand Russell
05-18.description: British philosopher and mathematician whose work on logic and analytic philosophy won him the Nobel Prize in Literature and whose anti-war activism made him a towering moral voice.

05-18.title: Tina Fey
05-18.description: First female head writer of Saturday Night Live who created 30 Rock and Mean Girls, reshaping American comedy with her sharp intelligence and feminist wit.

05-18.title: Mount St. Helens Erupts
05-18.description: The volcanic eruption in Washington State triggered the largest landslide in recorded history and a pyroclastic blast that killed 57 people and flattened 230 square miles of forest.

05-18.title: Napoleon Proclaimed Emperor
05-18.description: The French Senate proclaimed Napoleon Bonaparte Emperor of the French, consolidating his total hold on power after five years as First Consul.

05-18.title: U.S. Congress Passes Selective Service Act
05-18.description: Congress authorized conscription for the first time since the Civil War, rapidly expanding the American Expeditionary Forces sent to fight in World War I.

05-18.title: "This Is America" — Childish Gambino
05-18.description: Donald Glover's shocking music video alternating between joyful dancing and sudden gun violence became the most discussed piece of American art of 2018.

05-18.title: The Truman Show
05-18.description: Peter Weir's prescient satire about a man unwittingly born into a reality television show was remarkably ahead of its time and features Jim Carrey's finest dramatic performance.

05-19.title: Ho Chi Minh
05-19.description: Vietnamese revolutionary leader who founded the Viet Minh independence movement and guided North Vietnam through wars against French colonialism and American intervention.

05-19.title: Lorraine Hansberry
05-19.description: Playwright whose A Raisin in the Sun became the first drama by a Black woman produced on Broadway, unflinchingly exploring race, dreams, and family on the American stage.

05-19.title: Malcom X
05-19.description: Fiery civil rights leader and Black nationalist minister who advocated self-defense and Black pride, becoming one of the most electrifying and controversial voices of his era.

05-19.title: Anne Boleyn Executed
05-19.description: Henry VIII's second queen was beheaded at the Tower of London on charges of adultery and treason, just days before the King announced his engagement to Jane Seymour.

05-19.title: Marilyn Monroe Sings Happy Birthday to JFK
05-19.description: Marilyn Monroe delivered her breathlessly sultry rendition of Happy Birthday to President Kennedy at Madison Square Garden in a performance that became legendary.

05-19.title: Star Wars: The Phantom Menace Released
05-19.description: After 16 years of anticipation, George Lucas returned to the Star Wars universe with his CGI-heavy prequel, the most commercially anticipated film in Hollywood history.

05-19.title: "You Are the Sunshine of My Life" — Stevie Wonder
05-19.description: Stevie Wonder's sun-drenched declaration of love topped the Billboard Hot 100 and won him his first Grammy Award for Best Male Pop Vocal Performance.

05-19.title: Star Wars: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith
05-19.description: The darkest chapter of the prequel trilogy showed Anakin Skywalker's fall to the dark side, finally bridging the gap to the original saga with dramatic weight.

05-20.title: James Stewart
05-20.description: Hollywood's everyman hero whose drawling sincerity and moral conviction in It's a Wonderful Life and Mr. Smith Goes to Washington made him a beloved screen icon.

05-20.title: Honoré de Balzac
05-20.description: French novelist who mapped the entirety of French society in La Comédie Humaine, nearly 100 interconnected novels and stories that influenced Dickens, Zola, and Tolstoy.

05-20.title: John Stuart Mill
05-20.description: Influential British philosopher and political economist whose essays On Liberty and Utilitarianism remain cornerstones of liberal political thought.

05-20.title: Charles Lindbergh Departs for Paris
05-20.description: Lindbergh lifted off from Roosevelt Field in Long Island aboard the Spirit of St. Louis, beginning his 33.5-hour solo flight across the Atlantic Ocean.

05-20.title: Homestead Act Signed
05-20.description: Abraham Lincoln signed the Homestead Act, granting 160 acres of free land to settlers willing to farm it, fundamentally reshaping the settlement of the American West.

05-20.title: Amelia Earhart's Solo Transatlantic Flight
05-20.description: Amelia Earhart took off from Harbour Grace, Newfoundland, and landed in a Northern Ireland pasture the next day to become the first woman to fly the Atlantic solo.

05-20.title: "Jive Talkin'" — Bee Gees
05-20.description: The Bee Gees' syncopated funk crossover smash launched their greatest creative comeback and paved the way for their Saturday Night Fever domination.

05-20.title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
05-20.description: Tim Burton and Henry Selick's stop-motion dark fantasy, in which Halloween's Pumpkin King hijacks Christmas, became one of animation's most beloved cult classics.

05-21.title: Fats Waller
05-21.description: Jovial Harlem stride pianist and composer whose infectious wit and ebullient keyboard style on Ain't Misbehavin' made him one of jazz's most beloved characters.

05-21.title: Andrei Sakharov
05-21.description: Soviet nuclear physicist who helped build the USSR's hydrogen bomb but later became its most prominent dissident, winning the Nobel Peace Prize for his human rights advocacy.

05-21.title: Henri Rousseau
05-21.description: Self-taught French Post-Impressionist painter whose lush, dreamlike jungle scenes, though ridiculed by contemporaries, were championed by Picasso and became iconic.

05-21.title: American Red Cross Founded
05-21.description: Clara Barton founded the American Red Cross, modeled on the International Committee she had witnessed in Europe, launching a century of disaster relief work.

05-21.title: Charles Lindbergh Lands in Paris
05-21.description: After 33.5 hours and 3,600 miles, Lindbergh touched down at Le Bourget Field to a crowd of 150,000, completing the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight.

05-21.title: FIFA Founded
05-21.description: The Fédération Internationale de Football Association was established in Paris by representatives of seven European nations to govern the world's most popular sport.

05-21.title: Sour — Olivia Rodrigo
05-21.description: The teenage pop star's debut album turned her breakup into a cultural phenomenon, with Drivers License already a number one smash and the whole record radiating raw emotion.

05-21.title: The Empire Strikes Back
05-21.description: Irvin Kershner's sequel is widely considered the greatest Star Wars film, delivering Yoda, the Battle of Hoth, and the most shocking plot twist in blockbuster history.

05-22.title: Arthur Conan Doyle
05-22.description: Scottish physician and author who created the world's most famous fictional detective, Sherlock Holmes, and in doing so essentially invented the modern mystery genre.

05-22.title: Richard Wagner
05-22.description: Visionary German opera composer whose Ring Cycle and Tristan und Isolde redefined music drama, introducing the leitmotif and pushing tonal harmony to its breaking point.

05-22.title: Novak Djokovic
05-22.description: Serbian tennis champion who holds the all-time record for Grand Slam men's singles titles and spent a record total of more than 400 weeks ranked world number one.

05-22.title: Wright Brothers Receive Flying Machine Patent
05-22.description: Orville and Wilbur Wright were finally granted U.S. Patent No. 821,393 for their flying machine, three years after their historic first flight at Kitty Hawk.

05-22.title: Richard Nixon Visits Moscow
05-22.description: Nixon became the first U.S. president to visit the Soviet Union, signing the landmark SALT I arms limitation treaty and signaling a new era of Cold War détente.

05-22.title: Tokyo Skytree Opens
05-22.description: The 634-meter broadcasting and observation tower opened as the tallest tower in the world, offering sweeping views over the entire Tokyo metropolitan area.

05-22.title: There Goes Rhymin' Simon — Paul Simon
05-22.description: Paul Simon's third solo album blended gospel, rock, and New Orleans R&B in an exuberant collection that includes the sun-soaked masterpiece Kodachrome.

05-22.title: Raiders of the Lost Ark
05-22.description: Steven Spielberg and George Lucas introduced Indiana Jones in a breathless adventure that became one of the greatest action films ever made and launched a beloved franchise.

05-23.title: Carl Linnaeus
05-23.description: Swedish botanist who devised the binomial nomenclature system for naming species, giving modern biology its common language and earning the title Father of Taxonomy.

05-23.title: John Bardeen
05-23.description: American physicist and engineer who remains the only person to win two Nobel Prizes in Physics, for inventing the transistor and for the theory of superconductivity.

05-23.title: Margaret Fuller
05-23.description: American journalist and women's rights advocate who wrote Woman in the Nineteenth Century, the first major feminist work in the United States.

05-23.title: Joan of Arc Captured
05-23.description: The seventeen-year-old French military commander was seized by Burgundian forces at Compiègne, beginning the captivity that ended with her burning at the stake.

05-23.title: Java Programming Language Released
05-23.description: Sun Microsystems publicly released Java, the write-once-run-anywhere programming language that would power billions of devices and transform software development.

05-23.title: Anti-Mafia Judge Falcone Assassinated
05-23.description: The Sicilian Mafia detonated a half-ton bomb on the highway near Capaci, killing judge Giovanni Falcone, his wife, and three bodyguards in a brazen act of organized crime.

05-23.title: Tommy — The Who
05-23.description: The Who's groundbreaking rock opera about a deaf, dumb, and blind pinball wizard became one of rock's first double albums and remains the defining concept album of its era.

05-23.title: The Fast and the Furious
05-23.description: Rob Cohen's adrenaline-fueled street racing film launched one of Hollywood's most lucrative franchises, earning over seven billion dollars across its sequels.

05-24.title: Queen Victoria
05-24.description: Britain's longest-reigning monarch until Elizabeth II, whose 63-year reign oversaw the height of the British Empire and gave her name to an entire era of history.

05-24.title: Bob Dylan
05-24.description: Nobel Prize-winning singer-songwriter whose poetic folk and rock songs from Blowin' in the Wind to Like a Rolling Stone defined a generation's conscience and changed popular music forever.

05-24.title: John Wayne
05-24.description: Hollywood's archetypal Western hero whose stoic masculinity and laconic drawl made him the symbol of American frontier values in over 170 films.

05-24.title: First Telegraph Message Sent
05-24.description: Samuel Morse tapped out What hath God wrought from the Capitol in Washington to Baltimore, inaugurating the age of instant long-distance communication.

05-24.title: Brooklyn Bridge Opens
05-24.description: After fourteen years of construction and the deaths of twenty-seven workers, the Brooklyn Bridge opened as the longest suspension bridge in the world.

05-24.title: Star Wars: A New Hope Released
05-24.description: George Lucas's space opera opened in just 32 cinemas and quickly became a cultural phenomenon, breaking box office records and spawning one of the most valuable franchises in history.

05-24.title: Diamond Dogs — David Bowie
05-24.description: David Bowie's dystopian concept album, loosely inspired by Orwell's 1984, featured Rebel Rebel and marked his artistic transition from Ziggy Stardust to the Thin White Duke.

05-24.title: Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull
05-24.description: Harrison Ford strapped on his fedora again after 19 years for a fourth adventure that reunited him with Karen Allen and took the franchise into science fiction territory.

05-25.title: Ralph Waldo Emerson
05-25.description: American essayist and poet whose transcendentalist philosophy and call for self-reliance shaped American intellectual life and inspired countless thinkers and writers.

05-25.title: Ian McKellen
05-25.description: Celebrated British stage actor whose performances as Gandalf in Lord of the Rings and Magneto in X-Men introduced a generation to a legendary classical theatre career.

05-25.title: Igor Stravinsky
05-25.description: Russian composer whose three ballets The Firebird, Petrushka, and The Rite of Spring revolutionized twentieth-century music with their raw rhythmic force and harmonic daring.

05-25.title: Constitutional Convention Opens
05-25.description: Fifty-five delegates assembled in Philadelphia's State House to amend the Articles of Confederation and instead drafted the Constitution of the United States.

05-25.title: John Lennon and Yoko Ono Begin Montreal Bed-In
05-25.description: Lennon and Ono conducted their second famous Bed-In for Peace from Room 1742 of Montreal's Queen Elizabeth Hotel, recording Give Peace a Chance from the bedside.

05-25.title: Africa Day — OAU Founded
05-25.description: Representatives of 32 independent African nations established the Organisation of African Unity in Addis Ababa, creating the continent's first major pan-African political body.

05-25.title: Tubular Bells — Mike Oldfield
05-25.description: The debut release of Richard Branson's Virgin Records, this sprawling multi-instrumental opus was later immortalized as the theme music to The Exorcist.

05-25.title: Star Wars: A New Hope
05-25.description: The film that created the modern blockbuster premiered in just 32 theatres, its revolutionary space opera adventure instantly becoming a cultural phenomenon.

05-26.title: Miles Davis
05-26.description: Restless jazz trumpeter and bandleader who reinvented the genre at least five times, from bebop to cool jazz to fusion, always leading music into uncharted territory.

05-26.title: Lauryn Hill
05-26.description: Singer-songwriter who led the Fugees to global stardom and released The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill, still one of the most acclaimed albums in hip-hop and R&B history.

05-26.title: Helena Bonham Carter
05-26.description: Eccentric British actress of extraordinary range, from period dramas like A Room with a View to Tim Burton collaborations and her Oscar-nominated role in The King's Speech.

05-26.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average First Published
05-26.description: Financial journalist Charles Dow published the first Dow Jones Industrial Average, a market index comprising 12 companies that has tracked American capitalism ever since.

05-26.title: First 24 Hours of Le Mans
05-26.description: The first Grand Prix d'Endurance et de Consommation was held near Le Mans, France, launching what would become the oldest and most storied endurance race in motorsport.

05-26.title: Last Ford Model T Rolls Off the Assembly Line
05-26.description: After producing 15,007,003 vehicles over 19 years, Ford halted Model T production, ending the era of the car that put America on wheels.

05-26.title: Millennium — Backstreet Boys
05-26.description: The Backstreet Boys' second album sold a then-record 1.13 million copies in its debut week, cementing the boy band's global pop dominance at the turn of the millennium.

05-26.title: Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End
05-26.description: The epic conclusion of the original trilogy brought Captain Jack Sparrow and his allies to the edge of the world in a grand, action-packed maritime adventure.

05-27.title: Henry Kissinger
05-27.description: American statesman and diplomat who as National Security Advisor and Secretary of State shaped Cold War foreign policy with his doctrine of realpolitik.

05-27.title: Wild Bill Hickok
05-27.description: Legendary gunfighter, scout, and lawman of the American frontier whose mythologized exploits made him one of the defining figures of the Wild West.

05-27.title: Julia Ward Howe
05-27.description: American abolitionist and poet who wrote The Battle Hymn of the Republic, the rousing anthem that became the unofficial anthem of the Union during the Civil War.

05-27.title: St. Petersburg Founded
05-27.description: Tsar Peter the Great laid the foundation stone of the Peter and Paul Fortress on a Neva Delta island, establishing what would become Russia's grand imperial capital.

05-27.title: HMS Hood Sunk by the Bismarck
05-27.description: The German battleship Bismarck sank the pride of the Royal Navy in a matter of minutes at the Battle of the Denmark Strait, killing all but three of Hood's 1,418 crew.

05-27.title: SpaceX Dragon Docks with the ISS
05-27.description: The SpaceX Dragon became the first privately-funded spacecraft to dock with the International Space Station, opening a new era of commercial spaceflight.

05-27.title: Stadium Arcadium — Red Hot Chili Peppers
05-27.description: The Chili Peppers' double album finally gave them their first U.S. number-one album after more than two decades of recording, a sprawling rock triumph.

05-27.title: Moulin Rouge!
05-27.description: Baz Luhrmann's dazzling, anachronistic musical set in 1890s Paris dazzled with its pop song mashups and the electrifying chemistry of Nicole Kidman and Ewan McGregor.

05-28.title: Ian Fleming
05-28.description: British naval intelligence officer turned novelist who created James Bond, the suave secret agent whose twelve novels spawned the longest-running film franchise in history.

05-28.title: Jim Thorpe
05-28.description: Native American multi-sport athlete who won Olympic gold in the pentathlon and decathlon in 1912 and played professional football and baseball, widely regarded as the greatest athlete of his era.

05-28.title: Kylie Minogue
05-28.description: Australian pop princess whose irresistible disco-pop reinventions from The Loco-Motion through Can't Get You Out of My Head made her one of the best-selling female artists of all time.

05-28.title: Amnesty International Founded
05-28.description: British lawyer Peter Benenson launched Amnesty International from a letter in The Observer, creating the world's largest human rights organization.

05-28.title: Golden Gate Bridge Opens to Vehicles
05-28.description: The day after pedestrians first crossed it, San Francisco's Golden Gate Bridge opened to automobile traffic, its Art Deco towers becoming a global icon.

05-28.title: Greek Women Gain Right to Vote
05-28.description: Greek women were granted full suffrage and the right to stand for public office, with Eleni Skoura subsequently becoming Greece's first female Member of Parliament.

05-28.title: Oops!... I Did It Again — Britney Spears
05-28.description: Britney's sophomore album debuted at number one and broke the record for fastest-selling album by a female solo artist in chart history at the time of its release.

05-28.title: Braveheart
05-28.description: Mel Gibson's sprawling historical epic about William Wallace's Scottish rebellion won five Academy Awards including Best Picture and became a patriotic touchstone.

05-29.title: John F. Kennedy
05-29.description: The 35th and youngest elected U.S. President whose inspiring rhetoric, Cold War leadership during the Cuban Missile Crisis, and tragic assassination defined an American era.

05-29.title: Patrick Henry
05-29.description: American patriot and orator whose fiery Give me liberty, or give me death speech galvanized Virginia's delegates toward independence and made him a revolutionary legend.

05-29.title: Bob Hope
05-29.description: American comedian and entertainer whose USO shows brought laughter to millions of troops during World War II, Korea, and Vietnam over five decades.

05-29.title: Fall of Constantinople
05-29.description: Ottoman Sultan Mehmed II's forces breached the walls of Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire and the last vestiges of the Roman Empire after nearly 1,500 years.

05-29.title: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay Summit Everest
05-29.description: New Zealander Edmund Hillary and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay became the first people confirmed to reach the summit of Mount Everest, the highest point on Earth.

05-29.title: Rite of Spring Premiere Causes Riot
05-29.description: Stravinsky's savage, rhythmically violent ballet score caused a full-scale riot at its Paris premiere, dividing the audience into those who adored and loathed its modernity.

05-29.title: How Big, How Blue, How Beautiful — Florence + the Machine
05-29.description: Florence Welch's most orchestrally grand album debuted at number one in the U.S., her soaring vocals carrying songs of grief and longing to arena-filling heights.

05-29.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
05-29.description: Bryan Singer's ambitious time-travel epic united both casts of the X-Men franchise and became the highest-grossing film in the series at the time of its release.

05-30.title: Benny Goodman
05-30.description: The King of Swing whose integrated orchestra's Carnegie Hall concert in 1938 brought jazz to the concert hall stage and a national audience for the first time.

05-30.title: Idina Menzel
05-30.description: Broadway and film star who originated Elphaba in Wicked and gave the world Frozen's Let It Go, one of the most instantly recognizable songs of the 21st century.

05-30.title: Mel Blanc
05-30.description: Voice actor known as The Man of a Thousand Voices who brought Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Porky Pig, and hundreds of other Looney Tunes characters to irresistible life.

05-30.title: Joan of Arc Burned at the Stake
05-30.description: The nineteen-year-old French military heroine was burned alive in the marketplace of Rouen by the English-allied Burgundians, and was canonized 489 years later.

05-30.title: Lincoln Memorial Dedicated
05-30.description: The marble temple to Abraham Lincoln was dedicated in Washington D.C., with the President's son Robert Todd Lincoln among the guests at the ceremony.

05-30.title: SpaceX Crew Dragon First Crewed Flight
05-30.description: NASA astronauts Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley launched aboard SpaceX's Crew Dragon, the first crewed American spacecraft to launch from U.S. soil since the Shuttle's retirement.

05-30.title: Good Girl Gone Bad — Rihanna
05-30.description: Rihanna's career-defining third album introduced her harder, dance-pop sound and the global smash Umbrella, earning her a Grammy and making her a genuine superstar.

05-30.title: The Day After Tomorrow
05-30.description: Roland Emmerich's climate disaster spectacular froze New York City in ice and ignited mainstream conversations about climate change through spectacular destruction.

05-31.title: Walt Whitman
05-31.description: American poet whose Leaves of Grass, with its sprawling free verse and celebration of democracy and the human body, is the foundational text of American poetry.

05-31.title: Clint Eastwood
05-31.description: Hollywood legend who transformed from Spaghetti Western icon to Oscar-winning director of Unforgiven and Million Dollar Baby, one of cinema's most durable talents.

05-31.title: Joe Namath
05-31.description: Swaggering New York Jets quarterback who famously guaranteed victory in Super Bowl III and delivered, becoming the symbol of the counterculture athlete.

05-31.title: Big Ben Begins Keeping Time
05-31.description: The great bell of the clock tower at the Palace of Westminster struck for the first time, beginning the iconic Westminster chimes that have marked London's hours ever since.

05-31.title: Johnstown Flood
05-31.description: The collapse of the South Fork Dam unleashed 20 million tons of water on Johnstown, Pennsylvania, killing over 2,200 people in one of the deadliest disasters in U.S. history.

05-31.title: Adolf Eichmann Executed
05-31.description: Israel hanged Nazi official Adolf Eichmann for his role in organizing the Holocaust, the only time Israel has ever carried out the death penalty.

05-31.title: The Lion King: Original Motion Picture Soundtrack
05-31.description: Elton John and Tim Rice's songs including Circle of Life and Can You Feel the Love Tonight anchored one of Disney's greatest films and swept the Academy Awards.

05-31.title: Cleopatra
05-31.description: The most expensive film made up to that point starred Elizabeth Taylor as the Egyptian queen, its notoriously troubled production nearly bankrupting 20th Century Fox.
